implications_for_design: Every host reads controllers through SDL: Steam SDL3 3.4.0+, GFN SDL2 2.32.10, Shadow SDL2 2.24.2 (old). They also use the GameController/MFi path, and GFN additionally uses raw IOKit. A virtual pad has to satisfy the oldest of these, SDL2 2.24.2 in Shadow, and also avoid the double-enumeration that happens when both SDL HIDAPI and GameController see the same device.

Best-supported identity on this Mac is a dext-published (Transport USB, non-virtual) 045E:028E, version 0x0114. Copy Razer's descriptor exactly: 1 const byte, 16 page-9 buttons, Z/Rz 8-bit triggers, X/Y/Rx/Ry signed 16-bit, 6 pad bytes. It matches gamecontrollerdb's Mac 'Xbox 360 Controller' (360Controller) layout, which all three hosts ship. Never use version 0 or 1, the Steam-virtual markers that SDL ignores unless SDL_GAMECONTROLLER_ALLOW_STEAM_VIRTUAL_GAMEPAD is set. Caveat: Razer's own 028E is not seen in the Steam or GFN logs, so test this end to end before committing.

If GameController.framework support matters (Apple-native games, GFN's Forge path, and SDL's MFi path), the identity has to be one of the 14 GCIOMatchVirtual VID:PIDs. A CoreHID/IOHIDUserDevice pad as Elite V2 (045E:0B05, 0B22 or 0B02) or Series X (0B13) gets picked up by GameController even though its transport is Virtual. Elite V2 also exposes 4 paddles through GCXboxGamepad. DualSense Edge 054C:0DF2 is the other paddle-capable whitelisted identity, but it needs Get/SetReport feature handling for SDL HIDAPI PS5.

Two paths for the no-paid-account case. (a) Delegate publishing to OpenJoystickDriver, which is Developer ID with hid.virtual.device, through its records or identity picker; the user records folder does not exist yet. (b) For Shadow only, use ShadowUSB to forward the physical receiver to the Windows VM. The receiver then runs on native Windows/iCUE drivers with paddles and macros handled in-VM, needing no virtual pad at all.

Paid-account case: the Razer/iCUE pattern is the template. A dext matched on IOUserResources with an IOUserUserClient that spawns AppleUserHIDDevice children: a gamepad plus a keyboard/pointer for keyboard mapping and macros. Entitlements needed: driverkit, driverkit.family.hid.device, driverkit.transport.hid, plus userclient-access on the app. With Developer ID plus hid.virtual.device (both Steam and OJD have it), an in-process CoreHID publisher becomes possible too.

GDHub must detect ShadowUSB forwarding. When ShadowUSB has auto-forward saved for 1B1C:3A08, the receiver disappears from macOS, as the 'Device unplugged' and 'unforwarded' log lines show. GDHub should warn, or read /var/log/tech.shadow.shadowusb.daemon.log, and make the user choose between 'forward to Shadow' and 'GDHub virtual pad'.

Keyboard-mapping and macro output: CGEvent posting (needs Accessibility) is probably enough for Steam and Shadow. GFN reads raw HID keyboards in-stream (HIDKeyboardManager), so for GFN keyboard mapping needs a virtual HID keyboard (a dext like iCUE/Karabiner's, or IOHIDUserDevice with the entitlement). GFN does enumerate IOHIDUserDevice-class keyboards.

Steam tolerates a non-whitelisted generic usage-5 pad: the user binds it in Steam's controller setup, which saves to SDL_GamepadBind in config.vdf, and Steam Input then re-publishes its own entitled IOHIDUserDevice pad to games. In Steam the 'xbox mapping vs keyboard mapping' choice can therefore be handed to Steam Input. GFN and Shadow have no such layer and need a DB-recognized identity.

Avoid double controllers. If GDHub publishes a pad while Razer's 028E/27DB virtual devices or an OJD pad exist, hosts may enumerate several pads. Steam already showed the 8BitDo twice. Design a de-dup policy (one identity at a time; suggest disabling Razer's virtual controller), and mark GDHub's own devices with a distinctive serial number.

A live test with a GDHub-published 028E is needed.

Does the user hold a paid Apple Developer membership, possibly an organization one for INTERLINKED GROUP LTD, since an Apple Configurator cert exists? If so, can they get Developer ID plus a hid.virtual.device or DriverKit HID capability approved, and how long would approval take?

Does a CoreHID/IOHIDUserDevice pad posing as Elite V2 (045E:0B05 or 0B22) with Transport 'Virtual' get GCXboxGamepad paddles in GameController AND get accepted by SDL HIDAPI Xbox One in Steam and GFN? SDL treats the Virtual transport as non-Bluetooth and so takes the GIP report path.

findings.claim: macOS's own GameController matching table (AppleGameControllerPersonality.kext) decides which identities GameController claims. It accepts a VIRTUAL HID device (HIDVirtualDevice=true, i.e. CoreHID or IOHIDUserDevice) only for personalities flagged GCIOMatchVirtual=true. Those are: Xbox Wireless 045E:02E0, 02FD and 0B20 BLE; Series X wireless 0B13 and 0B23; Elite V2 0B02, 0B05, 0B22 and 0B3C; DualShock 4 054C:05C4/09CC; DualSense 0CE6 and Edge 0DF2; Switch Pro 057E:2009. 'Xbox 360 Controller' 045E:028E, Xbox Wired 02EA, Series X wired 0B12 and Elite USB 0B00 are matched WITHOUT that flag, so they need a non-virtual (dext-published) device.

findings.claim: In current SDL (main and Steam's SDL3), 045E:028E with version 0 is the Steam Virtual Gamepad marker on macOS. A device that carries kIOHIDVirtualHIDevice=true with that VID/PID/version is treated as Steam's own pad: SDL_ShouldIgnoreGamepad filters it depending on SDL_GAMECONTROLLER_ALLOW_STEAM_VIRTUAL_GAMEPAD. Non-virtual 028E devices are bumped to version 1. SDL main's GCController_SupportedHIDDevice also refuses every virtual device, and defers to GameController only on macOS 27.4+. This Mac runs 27.0.1, so in Steam both IOKit/HIDAPI and MFi can enumerate the same pad.
findings.evidence: SDL commits 'Detect steam virtual gamepads more accurately on macOS' (22 Feb 2026) and 'Fixed Steam Controller not detected on macOS under Steam' (May 2026). In main, SDL_iokitjoystick.c lines 650–655 and SDL_mfijoystick.m lines 1714–1729 contain '@available(macOS 27.4, *)'. Steam's controller.txt (26 Oct 2026) shows the 8BitDo opened twice: as HIDAPI 2dc8:202f and as GameController 05ac:0004.

findings.claim: Valve's own docs only say that on macOS 'emulated controller input is provided by a driver'. They give no macOS identity. The SDL DB entry 'Steam Virtual Gamepad, platform:Mac OS X' (GUID …8e02000001000000) and SDL's macOS marker show that Steam's Mac virtual pad presents as 045E:028E.
findings.evidence: The Steamworks Gamepad Emulation best-practices page contains the quoted sentence. The SDL2 and SDL3 DBs and GFN's embedded DB all carry the Steam Virtual Gamepad Mac entry.

findings.claim: The GeForce NOW Mac client (2.0.90.126, CEF-based) reads gamepads with a bundled SDL2 2.32.10 framework, which libGeronimo.dylib calls. It does not go through Chromium's Gamepad API. On this Mac the log shows 'Using SDLGamepad' and 'useForge: 0'. GFN also contains a GameController-based backend called 'Forge' (ForgeGCController and ForgeGCDeviceManager), switched on by a remote flag useForgeGamepadOnMacOS15Plus.
findings.evidence: otool shows libGeronimo.dylib linking SDL2.framework (current version 3201.10.0; Info.plist 2.32.10), GameController, IOKit and ForceFeedback. The CEF log has 'browser_app.cc(1152)] Using SDLGamepad'. geronimo.log has 'OS Supports Wired Xbox: 1 SDL Supports Wired Xbox: 1 useForge: 0', 'Loaded 315 gamepad mappings', and 'Opened controller named Ultimate 3 Controller with vendor id 5ac product id 4' (05AC:0004 is SDL's MFi label for a generic GCController). The strings include 'Skipping SDL gamepad for device %04x:%04x' and 'Skipping Forge gamepad for device %04x:%04x'.

findings.claim: In GFN's SDL2 2.32 stack, a pad is used only when SDL treats it as a GameController. That requires one of: (1) GameController itself supports the device (SDL2's IOS_SupportedHIDDevice calls [GCController supportsHIDDevice:] and does NOT exclude virtual devices); (2) GFN's embedded mapping DB matches the GUID (about 4,446 entries, 630 for Mac, none for 1B1C or 2E95; 045E:028E entries exist, with a version-agnostic fallback); or (3) an SDL HIDAPI driver claims it. A generic 1B1C usage-5 pad with no DB entry is therefore not a game controller in GFN. A 0B13/0B20/0B22-identity virtual pad is most likely seen through the GameController path.
findings.evidence: SDL2 branch: SDL_iokitjoystick.c JoystickAlreadyKnown hands off to IOS_SupportedHIDDevice; DARWIN_JoystickGetGamepadMapping returns SDL_FALSE (no automatic mapping); SDL_gamecontroller.c retries 'ignoring the version'; SDL_hidapi_xbox360.c on macOS rejects non-360Controller 028E unless it looks like the Steam virtual pad. GFN's DB strings include '030000005e0400008e02000000000000,Xbox 360 Controller…platform:Mac OS X' and the Steam Virtual Gamepad entry.

findings.claim: GFN on Mac reads the keyboard and mouse through raw IOHIDManager (HIDKeyboardManager / HIDRawMouseManager). That path is enabled on this Mac. CGEvent-synthesised keystrokes and mouse motion therefore probably do not reach a GFN stream; a virtual HID keyboard or mouse would. A fallback exists ('Skipping HIDKeyboardManager. Will use SDL_KeyboardEvents.'), and the binary imports IOHIDCheckAccess, so the fallback likely depends on Input Monitoring permission.
findings.evidence: geronimo.log has 'Enabling HIDKeyboardManager' and 'Enabling HIDRawMouseManager' 15 times each, plus 'Starting HIDKeyboardManager thread'. libGeronimo strings include the 'Skipping HIDKeyboardManager…' fallback; nm shows _IOHIDManagerCreate and _CGEventTapCreateForPSN. ShadowPCDisplay likewise has 'initKeyboardHID', a keyboardManager IOHIDManager and 'Input monitoring granted/denied' strings.
findings.source: local GFN logs and binaries; local ShadowPCDisplay binary

findings.claim: GFN has raw HID passthrough ('GSHID'), but only for a server-supplied allow-list of VID:PIDs. In this session that list was Thrustmaster 044F, Logitech wheels and flight 046D:C24F–C276, Saitek 06A3 and MadCatz 0738. 1B1C:3A08 is not on it. GFN can also synthesise a DS4 for the server from any gamepad ('synthesizedDS4FromGenericEnabled'; server reported 'Supports DS4: yes, DS5: no').
findings.evidence: geronimo.log has 'GSHID: Supporting {044F:0402}' … '{0738:A221}' and 'Configuring server supported Hid devices: Supports DS4: yes, DS5: no'. The strings include genericHidVidPidPairs, RIDevices.json and GamepadHIDSynthesizer.

findings.claim: NVIDIA's official macOS gamepad list: all Xbox Wireless controllers (Bluetooth or USB), Xbox 360 over USB, DualSense, DualShock 4, Logitech F310/F510/F710, and SteelSeries Nimbus/Nimbus+. 'Additional gamepads may work' but may need drivers. NVIDIA says nothing about virtual pads.
findings.evidence: System requirements page, macOS section.

findings.claim: Community reports on GFN Mac with third-party or virtual pads are thin and old. The recurring workaround, launching GFN as a non-Steam game so Steam Input supplies the pad, dates from about 2019. NVIDIA's own article suggests quitting Steam if PlayStation pads don't register. No report was found of OpenJoystickDriver, Razer or Karabiner virtual pads working in GFN Mac.
findings.evidence: Search results: NVIDIA GFN forum threads and the NVIDIA custhelp article a_id 5463.

findings.claim: The Shadow PC Mac client (Electron launcher 9.9.10481, plus a native CEF streamer ShadowPCDisplay.app 13.2.5) reads gamepads with a statically linked SDL2 2.24.2. It loads an external gamecontrollerdb.txt (2,203 lines; its SCUF entries are only 2E95:434B/434D/434E 'Scuf Envision' and 2E95:7725) and sends abstract gamepad state over its own GamepadChannel. GameController is weak-linked, used through SDL's MFi path. The Electron UI separately uses navigator.getGamepads(), but only to navigate menus.
findings.evidence: The binary embeds the build path '…/sdl2-2.24.2/SDL2-2.24.2/…'. The strings include ../../udu/src/sdl2/SdlJoystickInterface.cpp, GamepadManager.cpp, 'Ignore plugged gamepad named '{}'', '/gamepad/compatibility_mode' and Protocols::Controller::Client::Gamepad::Connect. A third-party gist confirms SDL2 2.24.2 and that SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG set through a launchctl setenv LaunchAgent is honoured.

findings.claim: SDL 2.24.2 (Shadow) predates macOS 15's native wired-360 support. On Sequoia and later, a wired 045E:028E can show up twice in Shadow (HIDAPI plus GCController). SDL issue #11002 tracks this, and the gist works around it with a dummy mapping.
findings.evidence: SDL issue #11002: a wired Xbox 360 controller on macOS 15.0 is detected by both HIDAPI and MFi. The fix landed in Oct 2024, after 2.24.2.

findings.claim: Shadow's USB forwarding on macOS is a root LaunchDaemon (/Library/ShadowUSB/ShadowUSB 4.6.2, tech.shadow.shadowusb.daemon, run with --ws --filter). It uses libusb plus SPICE usbredir over QUIC/websocket and exposes the device to the VM on an emulated UHCI port. It is installed and has ALREADY forwarded this receiver: 'Automatically forwarding device : SCUF Envision Pro Wireless USB Receiver V2 6940 14856' → 'UsbredirAddDevice : code=0, id=usb-8100 (protocol = UHCI)'. While forwarded, libusb holds the device exclusively, so the Mac (and GDHub) loses it.
findings.evidence: /var/log/tech.shadow.shadowusb.daemon.log, 2026-11-08 11:39–12:02. The pkg payload includes libusb-1.0.0.dylib, libusbredirhost.dylib and libusbredirparser.dylib. The strings include SpiceUsbDeviceForwarder and 'Do not save HID device {}, vid=…, pid=… for autoforward'.

findings.claim: Forwarding the receiver is fragile. Every time it re-enumerates (3A08 → 3A09 → 3A08 on link or idle change), ShadowUSB sees an unplug and the usbredir session dies ('device not responding', 'pipe is stalled', 'bulk transfer failed'). Only 3A08 is auto-re-forwarded. Forwarding also failed once with 'SetAlternateInterface: unknown error (0xe0005000)', most likely on the receiver's six USB Audio streaming interfaces (headset audio), which are isochronous and run over emulated UHCI. Whether iCUE inside the Windows VM actually worked is not visible from the Mac logs.
findings.evidence: Daemon log entries at 11:44:06, 11:46:47, 11:47:34 and 12:02:39. The receiver descriptor is 'class[9](Audio,Control Device)(Audio,Streaming)x6(Human Interface Device)(Human Interface Device)'.

findings.claim: Shadow's official guidance: forward controllers from Quick Menu → Controllers & USB (Alt+Cmd+O on Mac) after installing the USB drivers. Shadow can only detect controllers the local OS detects. A 'compatibility mode' emulates an Xbox One pad, and 'PlayStation controllers extended compatibility' emulates PlayStation pads as Xbox. Fully USB-forwarded devices are a separate path from the native gamepad channel.
findings.evidence: Shadow support search snippets and the controllers blog. Direct fetches were blocked (403/404).

findings.claim: OJD field results line up with the identity rules above. Its GameControllerCompatible profile appears in Steam as 'Xbox Series X Controller' with no input and no rumble. Its SDLCompatible profile (045E:0B0C over USB GIP) works in Steam and SDL but is invisible to GameController and Safari. Its Generic profile needs Begin Setup in Steam. OJD documents nothing for GFN or Shadow.
findings.evidence: OJD wiki 'Playing Games'.

implications_for_design: No single virtual identity is proven to work in all three hosts. The strongest single candidate is a DriverKit-published (non-virtual, Transport USB) 045E:028E 'Xbox 360 Controller' with version ≠ 0 (e.g. 0x0114, like Razer). macOS's GameController claims it natively (Xbox 360 personality, no GCIOMatchVirtual needed). Steam already opened Razer's identical pad via GameController on this Mac. GFN's SDL2 2.32 hands it to GameController, and its DB also has version-agnostic 028E mappings. Shadow's SDL2 2.24.2 sees it, with a possible duplicate. Cost: it needs the paid account plus the dext route, and it has no paddles.

Without a paid account (CoreHID or IOHIDUserDevice, so always Transport 'Virtual' and HIDVirtualDevice=true), only identities whose GameController personality has GCIOMatchVirtual=true reach GameController: 045E:0B13, 0B20, 02E0, 02FD, Elite 2 0B05/0B22, DS4 05C4/09CC, DualSense 0CE6. Use the libvirtualhid two-collection recipe (BT report 0x01 for GameController plus GIP 0x20 vendor collection for SDL HIDAPI/Steam). Never use 028E version 0, which SDL treats as Steam's own pad and filters. Avoid 028E virtual entirely: GameController won't take it virtual and SDL main drops virtual 028E.

For paddles, the Elite Series 2 identities (045E:0B05 BT or 0B22 BLE, GCIOMatchVirtual=true) are the most promising. GameController exposes Elite paddles, and SDL HIDAPI's Xbox One driver accepts the Elite 2 BT PIDs. Untested end to end. Option to evaluate separately: present as the SCUF Omega 1B1C:3A28. Apple's DB maps P1–P4, G1–G5 and S1/S2 for it, but it may not accept a virtual device, and Steam, GFN and Shadow have no SDL mapping for it.

Steam on macOS 27.0 with SDL 3.4+: expect double enumeration (HIDAPI or IOKit plus MFi) for pads that GameController also claims; GDHub's docs should tell users to disable the duplicate in Steam or rely on Steam's de-dup. A plain generic usage-5 HID pad is acceptable for Steam only after the user runs 'Begin Setup', but it fails GFN (no DB entry) and needs SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG for Shadow. Generic HID is a fallback, not a target.

GFN and Shadow both honour SDL's SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG environment variable (SDL2 reads it at init; the gist proves it for Shadow via launchctl setenv). If GDHub ever publishes a custom generic pad, it could offer an optional LaunchAgent that sets an SDL mapping for its GUID. This is a user-consented, persistent config change and needs explicit opt-in.

Keyboard mapping mode: Steam-launched games and Shadow probably accept CGEventPost keystrokes. GFN reads the keyboard and mouse through raw IOHIDManager (HIDKeyboardManager/HIDRawMouseManager enabled here), so CGEvent injection probably won't reach GFN streams. Plan a virtual HID keyboard/mouse (same entitlement or dext situation as the pad), or document 'deny GFN Input Monitoring to force its SDL keyboard fallback'. Test this first.

Macros should run in GDHub's mapping layer (timed sequences of virtual-pad reports or keyboard events), independent of host. GFN debounces nothing obvious, but SDL pollers sample at frame rate, so macro steps should hold each state ≥ 1–2 frames (~16–33 ms).

Shadow has an alternative path: USB-forward the receiver itself to the Windows VM, where iCUE gives full SCUF support with no virtual pad. ShadowUSB already did this successfully here. GDHub must detect it, because the receiver disappears from the Mac while forwarded, and should warn that every 3A08↔3A09 flip breaks the forward (only 3A08 is auto-re-forwarded) and that the six audio interfaces may fail over emulated UHCI. A possible feature: keep the receiver in 3A08 by keeping the link up, and show 'forwarded to Shadow' status instead of 'disconnected'.

GFN may later turn on its 'Forge' backend (GameController-only, remote flag useForgeGamepadOnMacOS15Plus). Whatever identity is chosen must also be claimed by GameController, not just by SDL IOKit or HIDAPI.
open_questions: Does a virtual (CoreHID) 045E:0B22 or 0B05 Elite 2 pad expose paddles in GameController (GCXboxGamepad.paddleButton1–4)? And are they read by Steam's SDL3 HIDAPI xboxone driver on the GIP 0x20 path, which has no paddle bytes in the libvirtualhid layout?

Will GameController accept a virtual or dext device for the 'dynamic' DB personality, i.e. SCUF Omega 1B1C:3A28 with paddles? Testable by publishing a dev dext or CoreHID device and checking GCController.controllers / ioreg GameControllerSupportedHIDDevice.

What condition triggers GFN's 'Skipping SDL gamepad for device %04x:%04x'? It could be a VID/PID deny-list fetched from the server or local de-duplication. Test by watching geronimo.log with the virtual pad connected.
Does GFN fall back to SDL keyboard events (and so accept CGEvent-injected keys) when Input Monitoring is denied, or are injected keys always ignored? Test with a CGEventPost key while streaming.

Is Steam's bundled SDL (3.4.0-1576-gab5541ec5) recent enough to contain the Feb and May 2026 Steam-virtual-gamepad changes and the macOS 27.4 GameController gate? This affects whether a virtual 0B13 shows once or twice in Steam on 27.0.

Did iCUE inside the Shadow Windows VM actually recognise the forwarded 1B1C:3A08 and its paddles? This is not visible from the Mac-side logs. Ask the user, or check Shadow's Windows-side device manager.
Does Shadow's 'Ignore plugged gamepad named …' filter suppress a virtual pad by name, for example to avoid doubling with USB-forwarded devices? Unknown which names it ignores.

Does a DriverKit-published 028E pad get rumble in GFN or Shadow on macOS? SDL routes rumble for GameController pads through GCController haptics; Apple ships Xbox360HapticCapabilityGraph.json, which suggests yes.

findings.claim: OpenJoystickDriver's dext publishes NO virtual pad. It is a USB transport driver that only claims physical Microsoft GIP/XUSB pads. OJD's virtual pads are published from the app process through the CoreHID virtual-device API, so they carry Transport "Virtual" and HIDVirtualDevice=Yes.
findings.evidence: The installed dext's Info.plist has IOProviderClass IOUSBHostInterface, idVendor 1118, and idProductArray [721,733,739,746,2816,2826,2834] (02D1/02DD/02E3/02EA/0B00/0B0A/0B12), class FF/47/D0. The dext entitlements are only driverkit + driverkit.transport.usb (those PIDs). The app's Developer ID profile 'OpenJoystickDriver DevID' (team 9PQP6CDMQT, individual 'Krystian Järveäär', created 2026-08-25, ProvisionsAllDevices) grants com.apple.developer.hid.virtual.device=true, and the signed app carries it. The binary contains 'CoreHIDVirtualDeviceDiagnostics' and 'Accessibility denied for IOKit virtual device'.
findings.source: Local: /Applications/OpenJoystickDriver.app (codesign -d --entitlements, security cms -D on embedded.provisionprofile, plutil on the dext Info.plist, strings)

findings.claim: Individuals can be granted the CoreHID entitlement com.apple.developer.hid.virtual.device with Developer ID distribution. Approval time varies widely, and there is no development-only variant.
findings.evidence: Granted: OJD (individual team 9PQP6CDMQT, profile dated 2026-08-25, checked locally) and OpenLogi (team 8U3ZJ258K9, signed agent verified on macOS 26.7). Pending: request H8Q3K9CK7Z, submitted 2026-06-30, was still 'Submitted' in Sep 2026 (DTS: 'some requests are taking a while at the moment'); macgip request K2QM957LZM, filed 2026-10-11, has no recorded outcome. libvirtualhid notes the entitlement is needed 'even for debug builds'.

findings.claim: In Apple's HID entitlement guide (Aug 2026), a dext that publishes a device through AppleUserHIDDevice needs com.apple.developer.driverkit + com.apple.developer.driverkit.family.hid.device. driverkit.family.hid.virtual.device is defunct. hid.virtual.device is CoreHID-only and 'should never be included in a DEXT'. A dext may publish any Transport string, and DTS says a dext has no advantage over CoreHID.
findings.evidence: The guide maps AppleUserHIDDevice -> family.hid.device, AppleUserHIDEventService -> family.hid.eventservice, IOHIDInterface -> transport.hid, and says 'include only the matching entitlement'. It also says 'location labels such as "USB" are just strings a driver publishes'. In thread 840311 DTS confirmed the virtual.device entitlement 'is not a valid entitlement'. In thread 845599 DTS was uncertain whether GameController will match a CoreHID pad.

findings.claim: With a paid Apple Developer Program account, the DriverKit 'Development Only' entitlement variants need no approval. They match broadly but run only on Macs registered in the profile when it was generated, and cannot be distributed. Distribution needs a separate request through developer.apple.com/system-extensions and Developer ID plus notarization.
findings.evidence: DTS (thread 818358, Mar 2026): dev-only variants 'match against a VERY broad hardware configuration' and are 'ONLY available to Development signed builds… will ONLY run on machines which were registered with your developer account at the point the signing profile was generated'. 'Everything else did/does have a development entitlement' (the PCI one was added late 2025). A forum answer states there is no approval process for the dev variants. A DriverKit development profile needs the Account Holder or Admin role, a DriverKit-enabled App ID, a dev certificate and selected devices. You cannot add entitlements to an existing profile; you must create a new one.

findings.claim: With a free (Personal Team) account, a dext can only be loaded by signing it 'Sign to Run Locally' and disabling SIP. In practice AMFI was also needed. DTS will not make an exception and advises against this on a machine you care about.
findings.evidence: Thread 847647 (Sep 2026), Kevin Elliott: 'disabling SIP should be sufficient, but if that doesn't work, disabling AMFI will'. The reporter needed AMFI off. 'The issue here is technical, not simply cost or policy': free accounts can't hold managed entitlements. Quinn: 'Do not disable SIP on a machine you care about.' On Apple silicon, turning SIP off puts the Mac into Permissive Security, set from recoveryOS. One macOS 27 beta 1 VM report said SIP would not disable. Its thread was resolved by signing with the entitlement, not by disabling SIP.

findings.claim: The app-to-dext user-client link is a separate restricted step. The app needs com.apple.developer.driverkit.userclient-access (requested per team or bundle ID), or the dext needs allow-any-userclient-access. A development variant of 'Allow Any UserClient' appears to exist, but this is not confirmed.
findings.evidence: Thread 849054 (Oct 2026): request userclient-access through the system-extension form, preferably as a team grant. Karabiner's README says userclient-access 'must be requested from Apple and cannot be granted automatically'. Search results show developers selecting 'DriverKit Allow Any UserClient (development)' on identifiers, with mixed reports.

findings.claim: Razer's DriverKit dext, already active on this Mac, publishes a non-virtual 045E:028E 'Xbox 360 Controller'. This is a working proof of the dext route and a template for the 360Controller-format identity.
findings.evidence: ioreg shows VirtualControllerDriverKit (class AppleUserHIDDevice, server com.razer.appengine.virtual.driver), VendorID 1118, ProductID 654, VersionNumber 276 (0x0114), Transport "USB", no HIDVirtualDevice key, DeviceUsagePairs 1/5. Its descriptor is 2 const bytes, 16 buttons, Z/Rz 8-bit triggers, X/Y/Rx/Ry int16 and 6 pad bytes, which is the 360Controller-kext HID layout. It has no output report, so no rumble. It is registered and active now, so expect it to appear as a phantom extra pad in hosts.

findings.claim: Third-party apps cannot drive the dexts already installed on this Mac (Razer, Corsair).
findings.evidence: Razer's virtual dext is signed with allow-any-userclient-access, but its user client logs 'Team ID does not match the expected value', so it checks the caller's Team ID. Corsair's VirtualHIDDeviceDriver has no allow-any-userclient-access.
findings.source: Local: strings of /Library/SystemExtensions/31507575-…/com.razer.appengine.virtual.driver.dext; codesign entitlements of the Corsair dext

findings.claim: GeForce NOW 2.0.90 on this Mac streams controllers through a bundled SDL2 2.32.10 (libGeronimo). It also has a GameController-based 'Forge' path chosen by remote config or macOS version. Logs show the SDL path was in use.
findings.evidence: otool shows libGeronimo.dylib and GeForceNOW link Frameworks/SDL2.framework (2.32.10) and GameController/ForceFeedback/IOKit. Strings include 'useForgeGamepadOnMacOS15Plus', 'Remote config forces use of Forge on all macOS versions', 'Skipping Forge gamepad for device %04x:%04x', 'supportsHIDDevice:', 'OS Supports Wired Xbox… SDL Supports Wired Xbox… useForge', 'failed to build a wired XBox 360 device', and an embedded gamecontrollerdb. The geronimo log for 2026-11-08 shows '[SDLGamepad] Closed a controller named Ultimate 3 Controller' (reported as VID 0x05AC PID 4, i.e. via SDL's MFi backend).

findings.claim: Shadow PC 9.9 reads controllers through a statically linked SDL2 2.24.2 in ShadowPCDisplay.app. It also ships a macOS USB Redirection daemon that could forward the physical receiver to the cloud VM.
findings.evidence: Strings contain the build path 'sdl2-2.24.2/SDL2-2.24.2' and the hints SDL_JOYSTICK_HIDAPI_*, SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG and '/gamecontrollerdb.txt'. The binary links IOKit, ForceFeedback and GameController (weak). native/shadowusb/ShadowUSB.pkg (notarized 2026-09-24) installs a root LaunchDaemon tech.shadow.shadowusb.daemon using libusb + usbredir. Shadow support says USB Redirection works on macOS and a forwarded device 'cannot be used outside of Shadow PC'.

findings.claim: Steam's macOS client handles controllers through a bundled SDL3 (3.4.0+1576, gab5541ec5) inside steamclient.dylib. That SDL3 contains the HIDVirtualDevice and 'GamePad-' checks. Steam knows Xbox Elite paddles 1–4.
findings.evidence: libSDL3.dylib reports the version string SDL-release-3.4.0-1576-gab5541ec5 and contains 'HIDVirtualDevice', 'GamePad-%d', 'supportsHIDDevice:'. steamclient.dylib contains 'Xbox Adaptive Controller', 'Xbox One Elite 2 Controller', '#origin_xboxone_button_paddle_1..4', 'SDL_GAMECONTROLLER_ALLOW_STEAM_VIRTUAL_GAMEPAD' and 'CControllerHidVirtualSocket'.

findings.claim: In SDL2, both 2.24 (Shadow) and 2.32 (GFN), the HIDAPI Xbox One driver on macOS accepts only Bluetooth PIDs and decides 'bluetooth' from the PID, not the transport. A Virtual-transport 0B0C or 0B13 pad is therefore parsed as Bluetooth report 0x01 in SDL2 hosts, while SDL3/Steam parses GIP 0x20. SDL2 2.24 reads Elite 2 paddles from report sizes 39 and 55.
findings.evidence: release-2.32.x: '#if defined(__MACOSX__) && defined(SDL_JOYSTICK_MFI) if (!SDL_IsJoystickBluetoothXboxOne(vendor_id, product_id)) return SDL_FALSE;' and 'ctx->bluetooth = SDL_IsJoystickBluetoothXboxOne(device->vendor_id, device->product_id);'. release-2.24.x is the same, with 'if (size == 16)' for the old format, 'size > 16' for the new one, and 'if (ctx->has_paddles && (size == 39 || size == 55))'. SDL2's IOS_SupportedHIDDevice has no kIOHIDVirtualHIDevice check; it differs from SDL3 here (brief §4b).

findings.claim: Consequence: OJD's 'SDLCompatible' identity (045E:0B0C, GIP 0x20 only) works in Steam but probably gives no input in GFN and Shadow. A 0B13 pad that carries Bluetooth report 0x01 (alone, or with the libvirtualhid dual collection) is the identity most likely to work in all three hosts.
findings.evidence: OJD wiki: SDLCompatible 0B0C 'Works' in Steam (macOS 27); GameControllerCompatible 0B13 is broken in Steam (no input) but works in GameController apps; SDLCompatible is 'Not seen' by GameController. The SDL2 code above parses 0x01 for any BT PID. libvirtualhid PR #208 (merged 2026-10-30) adds the BT 0x01 collection to the GIP 0x20 collection and verified GameController end to end; a reviewer noted 'Steam was not retested'.

findings.claim: GameController accepts a Transport-"Virtual" (CoreHID) pad that presents as 045E:0B13 with Xbox BT report 0x01 on macOS 26/27. Guide and Share do not surface.
findings.evidence: Two independent CoreHID publishers report it working: OJD (GameControllerCompatible 'Works… except Guide and Share'; Safari reads all buttons and rumble) and libvirtualhid PR #208 ('Verified end-to-end… Every face button, bumper, Menu/View, D-pad, stick click, both sticks, and triggers'). DTS calls GameController matching 'a little uncertain' in theory.

findings.claim: 045E:028E with the 360Controller report format is accepted by SDL2's HIDAPI Xbox 360 driver on macOS unless version == 1, which SDL2 treats as the Steam Virtual Gamepad. SDL3 treats version 0 as Steam's virtual pad. Version 0x0114, as Razer uses, avoids both. GameController does not support 028E.
findings.evidence: SDL 2.24 SDL_hidapi_xbox360.c: 'if (vendor_id == USB_VENDOR_MICROSOFT && product_id == 0x028e && version == 1) /* This is the Steam Virtual Gamepad */'. On macOS it accepts XBOX360 and XBOXONE types, excludes BT Xbox One, does not invert Y, and parses data[0]==0x00 reports: buttons in data[2..3], 8-bit triggers in data[4..5], int16 sticks in data[6..13]. Both GFN's and Shadow's gamecontrollerdb map 030000005e0400008e02000001000000 as 'Steam Virtual Gamepad'.
findings.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/libsdl-org/SDL/release-2.24.x/src/joystick/hidapi/SDL_hidapi_xbox360.c ; brief §4b ; local strings of libGeronimo and ShadowPCDisplay

findings.claim: OJD 0.6 (PolyForm Noncommercial from 0.6.0-alpha.2; MIT up to 0.6.0-alpha.1) supports user HID records that can map report 6, including paddle bits. It already does keyboard/pointer remapping, chords, sequences and turbo. OJD needs exclusive ownership of the physical device for virtual output, so GDHub cannot read the receiver at the same time.
findings.evidence: Controller-Records wiki: user records go in ~/Library/Application Support/OpenJoystickDriver/Controllers/VVVV-PPPP.json, apiVersion openjoystickdriver/v1alpha2, kind Controller, modes[].protocol.family HIDReportLayout. input.layouts[].report{id,length}, buttons[]/axes[]/hat[] use bitOffset/bitSize (bit 0 = LSB of byte 0); hat encodings are EightWay/Directions/Table; leftTrigger/rightTrigger; session.rumble.report{kind:Output,id,length}; modes[].match.interfaceSignature{usagePage,usage}; controls include LeftPaddle1/2, RightPaddle1/2 and Auxiliary1–8. Installed 0.5.0-beta.4 strings: identities '<generic-hid|sdl2-3|apple-gamecontroller|xbox360-hid|dualshock4|dualsense|switchpro>', 'Virtual gamepad output requires exclusive physical input ownership.', 'chord add… sequence add… --turbo-rate', and paddle1–4 labels. findings.claim: Karabiner-DriverKit-VirtualHIDDevice (Unlicense) is the best open-source DriverKit virtual-HID skeleton. It publishes only a keyboard and a pointer, needs root clients over a Unix socket daemon, and its README lists macOS 27 as Apple-silicon only. Building it needs your own DriverKit entitlements and profiles.
findings.evidence: README: license Unlicense (LICENSE.md). Entitlements: driverkit, family.hid.device, family.hid.eventservice, transport.hid, hid.virtual.device (the last two are unnecessary per DTS). Client socket: /Library/Application Support/org.pqrs/tmp/rootonly/karabiner_virtual_hid_device_service.sock. Rebuilding means replacing three provisioning profiles and team ID G43BCU2T37. Build needs Xcode 27+ and XcodeGen.

findings.claim: No host can see the raw receiver today, so a virtual pad will not show up twice alongside the physical device. Paddles can never reach GFN or Shadow games as paddles; they must be remapped locally.
findings.evidence: The receiver's IF3 primary usage page is 0xFF58; SDL's IOKit backend rejects a primary page other than GD, and GameController does not see it (protocol doc). GFN and Shadow forward an XInput-style pad to a remote Windows PC; XInput has no paddle fields (general knowledge, not checked against vendor docs).

findings.claim: Creating a CoreHID virtual gamepad triggers a TCC permission: Accessibility on older macOS, which libvirtualhid calls 'Device Control and Data Access' on current macOS. The grant must be in place before creation because a background broker cannot prompt.
findings.evidence: libvirtualhid docs: add the broker app under 'System Settings > Privacy & Security > Device Control and Data Access (Accessibility on older macOS)'. Brief §4a cites forum thread 820676 for the Accessibility/PostEvent prompt.

implications_for_design: DECISION MATRIX (route × account → Steam / GFN / Shadow; effort). R1 CoreHID HIDVirtualDevice inside GDHub, identity 045E:0B13, VersionNumber 0x0513, dual collection (BT report 0x01 + rumble output 0x03, then a vendor FF00/1 collection with GIP 0x20 + output 0x09), sending 0x01 then 0x20 every frame. FREE: not possible (restricted entitlement with no dev variant; only by self-granting with SIP and AMFI off). PAID: Steam ✓likely (SDL3 parses GIP 0x20 because transport≠BT); GFN ✓likely (SDL2 2.32 treats the PID as BT and parses 0x01, or goes through MFi/Forge GameController); Shadow ✓likely (SDL2 2.24 BT-by-PID 0x01, size>16 format). Effort: about 3–4 dev-days plus an approval wait anywhere from days to 3+ months.

R2 DriverKit dext (AppleUserHIDDevice, entitlements driverkit + family.hid.device, plus a user client) embedded in a GDHub .app. PAID: works immediately with Development-only entitlements, but only on this registered Mac, and is not distributable (fine for personal use). Identity A: 045E:028E 'Xbox 360 Controller', Transport USB, version 0x0114, 360Controller report plus an output report for rumble → Steam ✓likely, GFN ✓likely (SDL HIDAPI 360; the Forge path would skip it), Shadow ✓likely, GameController ✗. Identity B: 045E:0B13 with Transport 'Bluetooth Low Energy' and the BT descriptor → SDL2 and SDL3 parse 0x01 natively; GameController acceptance is speculative. Effort about 6–10 dev-days: new Xcode/XcodeGen project, .iig classes, user client, OSSystemExtensionRequest activation, approval UX, debugging. FREE: same code signed 'Sign to Run Locally', with SIP off (Permissive Security) and probably AMFI off (boot-arg). Host results are the same, but the security cost is large: Apple advises against it, and it should be done only on a test machine. Not recommended.

R3 OJD as the publisher (upgrade to 0.6.0-alpha.2, write ~/Library/Application Support/OpenJoystickDriver/Controllers/1b1c-3a08.json with HIDReportLayout for report 6). If bit 0 is the LSB of the report-ID byte: X/Y/Z/Rz at bitOffsets 8/24/40/56 (16-bit signed LE), LT 72 (10-bit), RT 82 (10-bit), hat 92 (4-bit EightWay table), buttons 1–19 at 96–114, paddles at extra bits 115–118, SAX at 119–120. Works the same with FREE or PAID accounts. Steam ✓ with SDLCompatible 0B0C (verified by OJD on macOS 27); GFN and Shadow likely ✗ with 0B0C but ✓likely with GameControllerCompatible 0B13, so the user must switch identity per host (`ojd virtual set …`). Effort 0.5–1 day. OJD's own keyboard mapping, chords, sequences and turbo apply. While OJD runs, GDHub cannot read the receiver (OJD needs exclusive ownership). Licence is PolyForm Noncommercial: fine for personal use, but it cannot be bundled into GDHub.

R4 keyboard/mouse output and macros from GDHub through CGEventPost (Accessibility TCC, no entitlement). Works with FREE and PAID accounts. Steam, GFN and Shadow all receive the keys when their window is focused, but the controller itself is not seen. Effort 2–3 days. It is needed in every plan for 'keyboard mapping' and 'macros'.

R5 Shadow-only: forward the receiver with Shadow's USB Redirection (the shadowusb root daemon, libusb + usbredir) so Windows SCUF/iCUE drivers handle it natively, paddles and iCUE macros included. Works with FREE and PAID accounts and needs no code. GDHub loses the device while it is forwarded. Untested for this composite audio + HID device at 1 kHz. R6: reusing the Razer or Corsair dexts is ✗ (Razer's user client checks the caller's Team ID).

RECOMMENDED PATH: (1) Now, on any account: add an output layer to GDHub with a MappingEngine that maps physical controls (including extra-bit paddles and SAX) to targets {virtual-pad control, key/key-chord, mouse, macro (timed sequence with press/release/delay, repeat, toggle, turbo), layer-shift}. Its sinks are a KeyboardMouseSink (CGEvent, ship first) and a VirtualPadSink protocol with backends CoreHID / Dext / None. (2) Move from `swift run` to a signed .app built with XcodeGen. Every entitlement, profile and system-extension route needs this, and it keeps the Accessibility TCC grant stable across rebuilds (a free 'Apple Development' cert is enough for that). (3) If the user has or buys the $99 membership: build the dext backend first, since it works today on this Mac with no approval wait. File the CoreHID capability request on the same day, and switch to the simpler CoreHID backend if it is approved (needed only for distributing to other Macs). (4) Ship two pad identities, selectable per host profile: 'Xbox Wireless' 045E:0B13 with the dual collection as the default (GameController + SDL2 + SDL3), and 'Xbox 360' 045E:028E v0x0114 as the fallback (SDL-only hosts). Never name the device 'GamePad-N', and never use version 0 or 1 for 028E.

FALLBACK if the user has no paid account and will not disable SIP: use OJD 0.6 with a 1b1c-3a08 record for 'controller visible' (0B13 identity for GFN and Shadow, 0B0C for Steam), plus GDHub's CGEvent keyboard and macro engine in a mode that does not open the receiver. Alternatively, GDHub could read OJD's published virtual pad with IOHIDManager as its input source so macros still run. For Shadow only, also offer USB Redirection.

Report builders to implement (pure, unit-testable like EnvisionProReport): Xbox BT 0x01 (≥17-byte firmware-5 layout; optional 39-byte Elite-2 form to carry paddles to SDL and Steam, speculative), GIP 0x20 (libvirtualhid byte map in brief §4b), and the 360Controller 20-byte report (data[0]=0x00, data[1]=0x14, buttons in data[2..3], 8-bit triggers in data[4..5], int16 sticks in data[6..13], no Y inversion on macOS). Scale the SCUF 10-bit triggers to 8 or 10 bits as needed. Forward host rumble (BT 0x03, GIP 0x09, 360 output) to the SCUF output report 0x09.

Paddles and SAX: GFN and Shadow forward XInput to Windows, so they must always be remapped locally (to an Xbox button, key or macro). Native paddles are only possible in Steam, SDL and GameController through an Elite-2-style identity, which is speculative; keep it behind a flag.

Host hygiene: Razer's dext-published 028E pad is active now and will appear as an extra (possibly player-1) controller in every host. The UI should detect it and warn, or the user can disable the Razer virtual driver under Login Items & Extensions > Driver Extensions. Steam may also add its own virtual 'GamePad-N'.

Acceptance-test plan for any route: SDL3 testcontroller; Steam Big Picture > Settings > Controller (check all inputs and rumble); the GFN in-stream overlay and the geronimo.log line 'Connected gamepad info … connectedGamepadInfoList'; the Shadow quick menu (ALT+CMD+O) > Controllers & USB, then a game inside Shadow; GCController.controllers() via a tiny Swift probe; and ioreg to confirm the Transport and HIDVirtualDevice keys.

findings.claim: GeForce NOW on this Mac reads keyboard and mouse straight from IOHID during a stream, through its own HIDKeyboardManager and HIDRawMouseManager. It does not use Cocoa/CGEvent input in that mode. A CGEventPost keystroke or mouse delta from GDHub is therefore very likely invisible to a GFN game while these managers run.
findings.evidence:
From ~/Library/Application Support/NVIDIA/GeForceNOW/geronimo.log (2026-11-07/08):
- 'INFO [CocoaInputController] - Enabling HIDRawMouseManager' and 'Enabling HIDKeyboardManager' appear at every stream start (12+3 times).
- 'Device added: <IOHIDDevice ... Razer Mouse Dock Pro PrimaryUsagePage=1 PrimaryUsage=6>' and '... Magic Keyboard PrimaryUsage=6' show it opens HID devices.
- It skips only the trackpad ('Skipping trackpad device').
From strings in /Applications/GeForceNOW.app/Contents/Frameworks/libGeronimo.dylib:
- 'keyboardManager:receivedKeyWithPage:usage:value:', 'rawMouseManager:mouseMoved:', 'IOHIDCheckAccess'.
- 'Skipping HIDKeyboardManager. Will use SDL_KeyboardEvents.' (the fallback when the HID path is off).
CGEventPost injects into the WindowServer stream and never appears as an IOHIDDevice report. So the HID managers cannot see it; this follows from the architecture and is not tested.

findings.claim: NVIDIA says GFN uses the Input Monitoring permission ('DIRECT MOUSE INPUT') for unaccelerated mouse input and low-latency keyboard access while the Streamer is frontmost. Without it, GFN falls back to the SDL/Cocoa event path. That fallback is the only GFN mode where CGEvent output would plausibly work.
findings.evidence:

- The permission is 'used only for unaccelerated mouse input and low latency keyboard access while the GeForce NOW Streamer is the active application'.

- Input mode shows 'alt' when active and 'sdl' on old versions.

findings.claim: Posting CGEvents needs no entitlement, but the user must approve it under Privacy & Security (Accessibility / PostEvent). Use CGPreflightPostEventAccess / CGRequestPostEventAccess to check and request. Preflight reflects the state at launch, and request is asynchronous. CGEventPost is ignored inside the App Sandbox, so GDHub must stay unsandboxed and ship outside the Mac App Store. One developer reports a rejection under guideline 2.4.5 for CGEvent.post.
findings.evidence: DTS answer on the Apple forums: 'Posting events with CGEvent does not require any specific entitlements. It does, however, require user approval in System Settings > Privacy & Security'. The same threads cover the preflight caveat and the sandbox behaviour. Input Monitoring (ListenEvent) is a separate permission for event taps, not needed for posting.

findings.claim: TCC grants follow the code-signing identity. When GDHub runs via `swift run`, TCC attributes it to the responsible app (Terminal/Xcode). An ad-hoc-signed rebuild changes its cdhash and loses the Accessibility grant. GDHub needs a real .app bundle signed with a stable certificate. A free Apple ID 'Personal Team' Apple Development certificate is enough, so no paid account is needed.
findings.evidence: Reasoning from how TCC designated requirements work; not re-verified on macOS 27.0.1. ARCHITECTURE.md says the app currently runs with `swift run` and has no Xcode project.

findings.claim: Karabiner-DriverKit-VirtualHIDDevice (pqrs) provides a real virtual keyboard and virtual mouse. It is signed by pqrs, free, released under the Unlicense, and lists macOS 27 (Apple Silicon only) as supported. Any app may use it through a header-only C++23 client that talks over a Unix socket to Karabiner-VirtualHIDDevice-Daemon, and the app need not be signed by pqrs. However, the client process must run as root.
findings.evidence:
From the README:
- 'This project implements a virtual keyboard and virtual mouse using DriverKit on macOS.'
- 'the virtual devices will only accept commands from processes running with root privileges.'
- The daemon lets apps reach the device 'even if the app is not signed with pqrs.org's code signing identity'.
- 'The daemon rejects requests with a different protocol version.'
- License: Unlicense. Supported OS includes 'macOS 27 Golden Gate (Apple Silicon only)'.
- Install: run the .pkg, then `Karabiner-VirtualHIDDevice-Manager activate`, approve the system extension, and run the daemon as root via launchd (ProcessType Interactive).
version.json: package 8.8.0, driver 1.8.0, client_protocol_version 7.
client.hpp API:
- async_virtual_hid_keyboard_initialize(parameters), async_virtual_hid_pointing_initialize().
- async_post_report() for keyboard_input, consumer_input, apple_vendor_keyboard_input, apple_vendor_top_case_input, generic_desktop_input, pointing_input.
- Signals: virtual_hid_keyboard_ready, virtual_hid_pointing_ready, driver_activated, driver_connected, driver_version_mismatched.
- Dependencies: pqrs dispatcher, unix_domain_stream, nod, asio.
pointing_input is buttons, x, y, vertical_wheel, horizontal_wheel, each 8-bit (relative deltas, ±127 per report).
The Karabiner dext is NOT installed on this Mac: `systemextensionsctl list` shows only the Razer x2, Corsair and OJD dexts.

findings.claim: Karabiner's virtual keyboard has historically shown up as VID 0x16C0 / PID 0x27DB with manufacturer pqrs.org. Since VirtualHIDDevice 5.0.0, the client can set the keyboard vendor_id and product_id (and country code) in virtual_hid_keyboard_initialize. The Razer virtual joystick on this Mac has PID 0x27DB too, which hints that Razer's dext derives from Karabiner's code.
findings.evidence: A gist of IOHIDKeyboardTester output shows 'Karabiner DriverKit VirtualHIDKeyboard 1.6.0' with VendorID=5824 and ProductID=10203. NEWS says 'Add vendor_id and product_id into the virtual_hid_keyboard_initialize parameters'. ioreg here: 'Razer DriverKit VirtualJoystic 0.0.3' vid=5426 pid=10203.

findings.claim: Client tools such as kanata (Rust) use the Karabiner virtual HID path in production, as GPL/LGPL tools without pqrs signing. The deployment pattern is: install the pqrs pkg, activate it, and run the daemon plus the client as root LaunchDaemons. Version drift between the installed daemon and the client headers is a known breakage source (for example, Karabiner-Elements 16.1 ships VirtualHIDDevice v8 while a crate targeted protocol 5).
findings.evidence: kanata release notes: 'sudo .../Karabiner-VirtualHIDDevice-Manager activate'. A community guide sets up two LaunchDaemons that 'must run as root'. The karabiner-driverkit crate issue describes the version mismatch.

findings.claim: The macOS 26.4 beta breakage of DriverKit virtual-HID tools affected seizing the built-in keyboard (input capture), not posting to a virtual keyboard. The reporter says it was resolved in a later seed. DTS pointed to CoreHID HIDVirtualDevice as the long-term replacement.
findings.evidence: Thread 817009: built-in keyboard events no longer reached DriverKit virtual HID tools; DTS mentions 'device seizer'; the OP says it was resolved in April 2026.

findings.claim: The Mac controller-to-keyboard tools found all use CGEvent: ControllerKeys/xbox-controller-mapper, Controlly, Joystick Mapper and Enjoy2/Enjoyable. None of them use virtual HID, so none can reach raw-HID consumers such as GFN in Direct Mouse Input mode. ControllerKeys needs Accessibility and adds a 'simulate key repeat while held' option. That option exists because synthetic keyDowns get no OS auto-repeat; a real (virtual) HID keyboard gets auto-repeat from the HID system.
findings.evidence:
ControllerKeys README:
- Uses 'Apple's CGEvent API'.
- Needs the Accessibility permission.
- Macros: Key Press, Type Text, Delay, Paste, Shell, Webhook, OBS, plus a JavaScriptCore scripting engine.
- Triggers: chords, long-hold, double-tap.
- Sensitivity/deadzone settings, calibration, and an RT precision modifier.
- 'Simulate key repeat while held' and 'Realtime Input Latency Mode'.
- License: PolyForm Noncommercial.
Other tools:
- Controlly needs Accessibility (App Store, 2021).
- Joystick Mapper is a paid App Store app with no confirmed Apple Silicon update.
- Enjoy2 is GPL.

findings.claim: reWASD (Windows only) and Steam Input both emulate keyboard and mouse. Valve warns that mouse emulation works only in games that accept mouse and gamepad input at the same time. On macOS, Steam Input keyboard/mouse templates apply only to controllers Steam itself sees, so for Steam games they depend on the virtual Xbox pad milestone.
findings.evidence: Valve's gamepad-emulation best-practices doc covers mouse emulation needing a game that takes mouse and gamepad at once. Forum fixes: per-game Steam Input override plus the 'Keyboard (WASD) & Mouse' template.

findings.claim: Games with mouse-look hide and disassociate the cursor (CGAssociateMouseAndMouseCursorPosition(false)) and read deltas. So a synthetic CGEvent mouse move must carry kCGMouseEventDeltaX/Y, and absolute positions alone fail. CGWarpMouseCursorPosition suppresses motion for about 0.25 s unless the suppression interval is zeroed. GFN logs 'AssociateMouse: 0/1' toggling, which confirms this lock and unlock pattern.
findings.evidence: Wine and SDL notes on the 0.25 s warp suppression (SDL zeroes the local-events suppression interval). Local geronimo.log: 'AssociateMouse: 1' x58, 'AssociateMouse: 0' x41, 'System mouse scaling: 0.687500'.

findings.claim: Native Mac games that read input through GameController's GCKeyboard/GCMouse or through IOHID get their data from HID devices, not the CGEvent stream. CGEvent injection probably does not reach them, while a virtual HID keyboard or mouse would. Games that use NSEvent (most SDL, Unity and Electron/Chromium apps, including the Steam client UI) do receive CGEvents.
findings.evidence: Search found no source that states this directly. It is inferred from the architecture: GCMouse supplies raw HID deltas, and GFN's own split between a HID path and an SDL path is an example. Steam game coverage per engine is unknown.

findings.claim: Secure Event Input (password fields, Terminal 'Secure Keyboard Entry') mainly stops event taps from observing keys. Objective-See reports that newer macOS protects only specific UI, such as security prompts, against synthetic clicks. How CGEventPost keystrokes behave under secure input on macOS 27 is unverified. A HID-level virtual keyboard is not affected the way taps are.
findings.evidence: Patrick Wardle, 'Synthetic Reality': the defences 'protect only certain UI components'. One Apple forum report logs 'Sender is prohibited from synthesizing events'.

findings.claim:
Stick-to-mouse practice from DS4Windows and Steam Input:
- A linear curve feels bad. An 'Enhanced Precision' or quadratic ease-in curve is preferred.
- Disabling the inner deadzone causes constant drift.
- Steam offers a custom response curve plus an outer-ring 'edge spin' (keep turning at full deflection).
No standard exponent parameter is documented.
findings.evidence: DS4Windows guide: curves (Linear, Enhanced Precision, Quadratic), deadzone/anti-deadzone/maxzone. Steam forum threads on the mouse-joystick custom curve, edge spin, and the drift seen with no deadzone.

findings.claim: Mouse motion through a virtual HID pointer differs from motion through CGEvent. A virtual HID pointer's deltas go through macOS pointer acceleration for the cursor (GFN logs 'System mouse scaling: 0.6875'), but raw-HID readers (GFN Direct Mouse Input, GCMouse) get them unaccelerated. A CGEvent with an explicit location is not accelerated further. So sensitivity has to be set per backend and per host.
findings.evidence: Reasoning from the HID event pipeline and NVIDIA's 'unaccelerated mouse input' wording, plus the local log.

implications_for_design:
Add an output-sink abstraction under Mapping. A protocol `InputSink`, with keyDown/keyUp(HIDUsage), mouseButton, mouseDelta(dx,dy), scroll, gamepadState and releaseAll, has three implementations:
(a) CGEventSink: no install needed; needs Accessibility/PostEvent.
(b) VirtualHIDSink: Karabiner-DriverKit-VirtualHIDDevice through a root helper.
(c) VirtualGamepadSink: from the gamepad milestone.
The mapping and macro engine sits above the sinks and stays independent of them.

Recommend the virtual HID route (Karabiner dext) as the primary keyboard/mouse output for streaming hosts and games, with CGEvent as the zero-install fallback:
- GFN reads raw HID while Direct Mouse Input / Input Monitoring is on, as seen on this Mac.
- Games that use GCKeyboard/GCMouse also read HID.
- The Karabiner route needs no paid Apple account: pqrs signs the dext, the license is the Unlicense, and macOS 27 Apple Silicon is listed as supported.
- If the user keeps CGEvent output, tell them to turn off GFN's Direct Mouse Input / Input Monitoring so GFN falls back to SDL/Cocoa events. The cost is accelerated mouse and slightly higher key latency.

The Karabiner client must run as root. Ship a tiny root helper (C++ or Swift with the header-only C++23 client) as a LaunchDaemon. With no paid account, install it with an admin-authorized script; with Developer ID signing, SMAppService.daemon may work. GDHub (the user process) sends compact key/mouse messages over an XPC or Unix socket with audit-token / code-signature checks on the caller. Without that check the helper is a system-wide keystroke-injection backdoor.

Pin client_protocol_version 7 (package 8.8.0, driver 1.8.0). Handle the driver_version_mismatched, driver_activated and driver_connected signals and show them in the UI. If Karabiner-Elements is installed, it already ships and runs the same dext and daemon: reuse it rather than install a second copy, and expect version drift after KE updates.

Store key bindings as HID usages (page 0x07, plus consumer page 0x0C for media keys) as the canonical key identity. Convert to CGKeyCode for the CGEvent sink. Both are layout-independent physical positions. The user's layout is British/ISO (GFN log: com.apple.keylayout.British), so set the Karabiner keyboard country_code/keyboard type to ISO and test the §/` and \| keys (kVK_ISO_Section, HID 0x64 vs 0x35 swap).

CGEvent sink details:
- Use a CGEventSource(.hidSystemState) and post at kCGHIDEventTap.
- Post explicit flagsChanged events for modifiers and set CGEventFlags on every key event.
- While a mouse button is held, post LeftMouseDragged (or the matching drag type) instead of MouseMoved.
- Always fill kCGMouseEventDeltaX/Y. Clamp the location to the display union, and never warp, so locked-cursor games and Shadow's relative mode get deltas.
- Synthesize key auto-repeat only when a profile asks for it (synthetic keys get no OS auto-repeat; the virtual HID keyboard does).

Stick-to-mouse pipeline, run on a fixed 500–1000 Hz high-QoS timer separate from the 1 kHz report callback:
- Normalize with the learned AxisRange.
- Radial inner deadzone (default about 0.10) and outer saturation (about 0.95), rescaled to 0..1.
- Response curve v = m^γ (γ default 2.0, range 1–3) or a piecewise 'precision' curve.
- Optional edge-acceleration ramp: after more than 150 ms above 0.95, ramp the multiplier to 1.5–2.5x over about 300 ms.
- Max speed in px/s × sensitivity, plus a hold-to-slow precision modifier.
- Carry sub-pixel remainders between ticks.
- For the Karabiner pointer, split deltas so each report stays within ±127.
- Keep separate sensitivity presets for the CGEvent and virtual HID backends, because macOS acceleration applies to the virtual HID pointer's cursor but not to raw readers.
Scroll from a stick or buttons: smooth pixel scrolling via CGEventCreateScrollWheelEvent2 (CGEvent sink) or wheel ticks in pointing_input (virtual HID). Make the rate depend on deflection.

Macro engine (output-agnostic):
- Steps: key down/up/tap, text, mouse button, mouse move, scroll, delay, gamepad button/axis on the virtual pad, profile/layer switch.
- Triggers: press, release, hold, long-press, double-tap, toggle, turbo/rapid-fire at N Hz, chords. Paddles or SAX work well as layer-shift keys.
- Run on a dedicated serial queue with mach-absolute timing.
- Make it cancellable on re-trigger.
- Release every held key and button on controller sleep (stream stop), 0x3A09 idle, profile switch, app quit or crash (watchdog in the helper), and when Accessibility is revoked. This prevents stuck keys.

Per-app automatic profiles keyed on the frontmost bundle id:
- com.nvidia.gfnpc.streamer and com.blade.shadow-macos (the stream windows)
- com.nvidia.gfnpc.mall and com.electron.shadow (the launchers)
- com.valvesoftware.steam and the game's own bundle id
Each profile chooses Xbox output, keyboard/mouse output, or mixed.

Avoid double input: when a control maps to keyboard/mouse, leave it neutral in the virtual pad report. In a pure keyboard/mouse profile, don't publish the virtual pad at all. Consider seizing the SCUF interface (kIOHIDOptionsTypeSeizeDevice) so SDL hosts such as GFN's SDL2 and Steam don't also see the raw usage-5 gamepad collection.

Package GDHub as a signed .app bundle with a stable certificate (a free Personal Team Apple Development cert is enough). That keeps Accessibility/PostEvent grants across rebuilds. `swift run` attributes TCC to Terminal. Keep it unsandboxed and distribute outside the Mac App Store.

Paid-account path: GDHub's own DriverKit dext could publish one composite device (Xbox gamepad + keyboard + mouse collections), replacing both the Karabiner dependency and the gamepad route from the prior-art brief §4. CoreHID HIDVirtualDevice can also publish a keyboard/mouse once the restricted entitlement is granted. Either way, design the sink protocol now so a backend can be swapped in later.
Macros in online multiplayer games may break a game's terms of service. Surface a non-blocking note in the macro UI. This is a policy consideration and was not researched.
