findings.claim: GDHub's current input path delivers every 1 kHz report to the main thread. That suits the UI but not a deterministic output engine. The engine needs its own serial queue fed by timestamped reports.
findings.evidence: HIDMonitor.swift schedules devices on CFRunLoopGetMain (common modes) and wraps each input report in DispatchQueue.main.async { MainActor.assumeIsolated { onInputReport } }. EnvisionProDevice.handle then parses, logs and diffs on the MainActor. The SDK header (MacOSX.sdk IOHIDDevice.h) declares IOHIDDeviceSetDispatchQueue as __OSX_AVAILABLE(10.15). It says a device 'should not be associated with both a runloop and dispatch queue' and must be started with IOHIDDeviceActivate. IOHIDDeviceRegisterInputReportWithTimeStampCallback is declared AVAILABLE_MAC_OS_X_VERSION_10_10_AND_LATER and passes a mach-time timestamp.

findings.claim: The existing ControlMapping answers 'which HID field is which physical control', not 'what the control does'. Its JSON uses Swift's synthesized enum coding, which makes a poor base for an editable profile format. The action model should therefore be a separate, versioned schema that refers to the same layout control ids.
findings.evidence: ControlMapping has buttons: [String: Binding] (.button/.hat/.trigger/.axis), sticks with learned AxisRange extremes, and physicalBits (the extra-bit masks for paddles and SAX). The saved ~/Library/Application Support/GDHub/envision-pro-mapping.json encodes these as {"a":{"button":{"_0":1}}}. The layout control ids are lt, lb, sax_left, dpad_up/right/down/left, left_stick, l3, view, start, profile, g1–g5, menu, a, b, x, y, right_stick, r3, sax_right, rb, rt, paddle_outer_left, paddle_inner_left, paddle_inner_right, paddle_outer_right. Each has a kind (button/stick/trigger) and a view (front/back/sideLeft/sideRight).

findings.claim: Paddles and SAX buttons also echo their on-controller function into the standard fields, so independent remapping needs an echo-suppression stage. The current code lights the paddle hotspot from its physical bit, but it does not stop the face control (A, B or a D-pad direction) from also reading as pressed.
findings.evidence: The protocol doc says the standard fields carry the onboard-profile function (in the factory profile, paddles are the D-pad and SAX are A/B), while extra bits 0–5 carry physical identity. ControlMapping.isActive gives the physical bit precedence only for the paddle's own id. 'a' is still active whenever button 1 is high, including when SAX-left is pressed. B3Mac's decoder attributes on edges: every standard button that rises in the same report as an extra input's rising edge is recorded as its echo and subtracted until that input is released. Buttons already held, or pressed later, pass through. Its stated limitation is that a real face press landing in the same report is also suppressed.

findings.claim: Both cloud clients installed here read gamepads through SDL. GeForce NOW links SDL2.framework 2.32.10. Shadow's streaming binary (ShadowPCDisplay, com.blade.shadow-macos) embeds SDL and weak-links GameController. Gamepad visibility in both therefore follows SDL's acceptance rules, while keyboard and mouse come through the normal macOS event stream.
findings.evidence: otool -L /Applications/GeForceNOW.app/Contents/MacOS/GeForceNOW shows @executable_path/../Frameworks/SDL2.framework (current version 3201.10.0), and the framework's Info.plist reports 2.32.10. otool -L on ShadowPCDisplay shows IOKit, Carbon and GameController (weak). Its strings include SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG, SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG_FILE, LoadDefaultGameControllerDb, SDL_JOYSTICK_HIDAPI and SDL_JOYSTICK_HIDAPI_PS5. The Shadow shell is com.electron.shadow 9.9.10481 and GeForce NOW is com.nvidia.gfnpc.mall 2.0.90.126.

findings.claim: GeForce NOW per-game shortcuts are JSON deep links into the same app, not separate processes. Auto-switching per game inside GeForce NOW or Shadow cannot rely on bundle id alone; it needs a window-title rule or a manual pin.
findings.evidence: '/Applications/Dune Awakening on GeForce NOW.gfnpc' contains {"url-route":"#?cmsId=102371911&launchSource=External&shortName=..."}. The World of Warcraft shortcut has the same shape. DS4Windows and JoyToKey both added window-title matching for exactly this kind of shared-host case. DS4Windows cites Windows Store apps that share applicationFrameHost.exe.

findings.claim: Steam on this Mac already stores hand-made SDL gamepad bindings and has seen Xbox One and generic controllers. A stale per-GUID binding would be applied silently to any virtual pad whose GUID matches.
findings.evidence: ~/Library/Application Support/Steam/config/config.vdf line 620 has "SDL_GamepadBind" with entries for GUID 050000005e040000e002000043c96d04 ('Xbox 360 Controller', with non-standard a:b0,b:b1,x:b5,y:b6,...) and 05000000ac05000004000000503f6d04 ('Ultimate 3 Controller'). A userdata localconfig.vdf has "ControllerTypesUsed" "controller_ps5,controller_xboxone,controller_generic,". The per-type 'Steam Input for Xbox controllers' toggle was not found in the local vdf files.

findings.claim: A normal user-space app can seize (exclusively open) a non-keyboard HID device. Other IOHIDLib clients, such as Steam's and SDL's HIDAPI in GeForce NOW and Shadow, then stop receiving its reports, and get them back when the seizer closes. This is the macOS equivalent of reWASD's 'Hide physical controller'.
findings.evidence: In IOHIDLibUserClient::open, an unprivileged client is refused only when the device is a keyboard and it asks to seize: '__Require_Action(!fNubIsKeyboard || ((options & kIOHIDOptionsTypeSeizeDevice) == 0) ...'. When another client seizes, existing clients get kIOMessageServiceIsRequestingClose and set fClientSeized=true and setValid(false). handleEnqueue skips seized clients. kIOMessageServiceWasClosed restores them. reWASD hides the physical pad when a virtual one is added so that both do not report input: 'Hide physical controller when the virtual one is added'.

findings.claim: Posting keyboard and mouse events with CGEvent needs no entitlement and no paid developer account. The only requirement is user approval of the PostEvent TCC service, which appears under Privacy & Security > Accessibility but is separate from full Accessibility. It can be checked with CGPreflightPostEventAccess and requested with CGRequestPostEventAccess (macOS 10.15+). This makes keyboard mapping shippable now in Steam, GeForce NOW and Shadow, independent of the virtual-pad entitlement problem.
findings.evidence: Apple DTS: 'Posting events with CGEvent does not require any specific entitlements. It does, however, require user approval'. DTS also says the grant is 'just limited to posting events' and that tccutil has separate services for Accessibility, ListenEvent and PostEvent. The SDK's CGEvent.h declares CGPreflightPostEventAccess/CGRequestPostEventAccess API_AVAILABLE(macos(10.15)). CGEventTypes.h defines kCGMouseEventDeltaX=4 and kCGEventSourceUserData=42, used for relative mouse and for tagging GDHub's own events.

findings.claim: Each rebuild of the bundled app is ad-hoc signed, so a granted PostEvent permission will probably not survive rebuilds. No Apple Development identity exists in the keychain yet. A stable signing identity (a free Personal Team certificate or a self-signed code-signing certificate) is needed for practical keyboard-output development, whether or not the user has a paid account.
findings.evidence: scripts/bundle.sh runs 'codesign --force --sign - "$APP"' on every build. `security find-identity -v -p codesigning` lists only an 'Apple Configurator: INTERLINKED GROUP LTD' identity. Inferred, not tested: TCC ties an ad-hoc binary's grant to its cdhash, which changes on every build.

findings.claim: The best-documented activator model to copy is Steam Input's. Its types are Regular, Double, Long, Start, Release and Chorded press. Its settings are Toggle, Fire Start Delay, Fire End Delay, Haptics, Cycle Binding, Interruptible, Double Tap Time, Long Press Time, Hold to Repeat (turbo) and Repeat Rate. It defines exact conflict rules between activators on the same button.
findings.evidence: Steam's activator settings page: Long Press 'requires the button to be held for a period of time to activate' and 'will stay active until you release it'. 'Any interruptable activators also on this input will not be activated until the button is released prior to this time and they will not be activated at all if the Long Press is activated.' Double Press pauses interruptible activators until the double-tap time passes. Start Press activates on press and deactivates even while held. Release Press activates and deactivates on release. Chorded Press needs another button held, and 'Other bindings for the chorded button will continue to fire.' Interruptible exists only on Regular and Release; turbo exists on Regular, Double and Long. Ranges are 0.0–1.0, and the example uses a 0.15 s long press.

findings.claim: reWASD adds Triple Press. It always fires Start Press first and Release Press last. It records a real cost: a button that also has a Long or Double activator delays its single press, because the tool must wait to know which activator will win.
findings.evidence: reWASD help: Start Press 'reproduces right after the button is pressed' and always fires first. Release Press 'reproduces once the button is released'. Long Press conflicts with a Hold-until-release Single Press because 'reWASD will always detect the Long Press'. Press counts reset after an activator completes. A reWASD forum reply explains that with several activators on one button, reWASD 'needs to be sure which activator is going to work next, and so there is truly a delay'. ControllerKeys on macOS offers a 'Realtime mode' that 'sends simple key mappings as key-down on press and key-up on release', bypassing its chord window.

findings.claim: Layers have converged across tools. A layer is a sparse overlay that inherits unbound controls from the base unless a control is explicitly set to 'do not inherit'. It is entered by hold (shift), toggle, or one-way/two-way switching. The shift button's own binding inside the target layer is suppressed while it is held.
findings.evidence: reWASD: up to 10 shift layers. An unmapped control 'will reproduce as a mapping from Main layer' unless 'Do not inherit' is chosen. Jump modes are Hold, Toggle and Custom (separate exit buttons). Options include 'Delay before Jump' and 'Postpone the mapping'. A layer that never returns to Main can get the user stuck; the escape is an emergency remap-off shortcut, Ctrl+Alt+Del. AntiMicroX: 8 sets per profile with selector modes One Way, Two Way and While Held. With While Held, 'the button's slots in the original set do not fire' and releasing it restores the original set. Xbox Accessories (Elite Series 2): each button has a 'Primary usage' and a 'Shift mode usage'. ControllerKeys (macOS): 'Up to 12 additional layers per profile', activated by Hold or Toggle. JoyToKey 5.8.2 added a delayed shift, so one button can send a key on a short press and act as SHIFT on a long press.

findings.claim: Outputs already held when a layer changes need an explicit policy. In Steam, a mode shift reportedly does not interrupt a held button, while an action layer does.
findings.evidence: A Steam community side-by-side test: 'the mode shift does not interrupt input from the "A Button", whereas the action layer does.' Users also report layers getting stuck when an Add Layer has no matching Remove. This comes from community posts, not Valve documentation.

findings.claim: Macro semantics from prior art are as follows. reWASD separates 'Hold until release' (keys go down together and up on release; pauses play only while held) from 'Execute at once' (ordered down/up/pause steps, Iterations, Pause between iterations, recommended delay between keys ≥20 ms). It also has Combo break, Rumble and stick-deflection (Absolute/Relative) elements, and recording. DS4Windows macros offer Record delays, scan codes, Play once vs Repeat while held, Insert wait and Add rumble. AntiMicroX slots add Pause, Hold, Release, Cycle (with auto-reset), Distance, Delay, Press Time (default 0.10 s) and Mouse Mod.
findings.evidence: reWASD key-combo help: Pause 'up to almost 12 hours'. A combo break means 'the combo will stop reproducing after each break, and continue once the button is pressed again' (up to 32 breaks). With Rumble, 'all the other keys that are after it ... will reproduce once Rumble is finished'. Delay between keys: 'at least a 20 milliseconds'. DS4Windows RecordBox.xaml localization keys: RecordBox.RecordDelays, ScanCode, RecordBox.PlayOnce, RecordBox.RepeatWhileHeld, RecordBox.InsertWait, RecordBox.AddRumble, RecordBox.ChangeLightbarColor. AntiMicroX wiki: Release 'Multiple Release zones add their times together'; Hold releases slots activated before it; Delay keeps them active; Distance can be used at e.g. 80% for walk/run.

findings.claim: Analog conditioning in prior art works like this. Use a scaled radial deadzone so precision near the deadzone edge is not lost. Add an outer (max) zone and an anti-deadzone for pad output to cancel the game's own deadzone. Offer preset curves (Linear, Enhanced Precision, Quadratic, Cubic, Easeout, Custom 4-point bezier). reWASD adds Low/Medium/High stick and trigger zones for distance-based bindings. Steam triggers use a soft-pull point (about 30.5% default per community) and hip-fire modes.
findings.evidence: Sutphin: stickInput.normalized * ((stickInput.magnitude - deadzone) / (1 - deadzone)), with typical thresholds of 0.1–0.2. AntiMicroX Enhanced Precision: 0–40% of travel at 0.405x, linear to 80%, accelerated above. Its Easing Quadratic/Cubic presets ramp to full speed over 0.75 s in the top band. DS4Windows defines anti-deadzone as the minimum output after leaving the deadzone, and its custom curve is a 4-number bezier. reWASD: zones are Deadzone, Low, Medium and High, shaped Radial or Elliptic (Elliptic only for keyboard mappings). Steam community: Soft Pull Point defaults to 30.5%; Hip Fire delays the soft pull so that a quick full pull skips it. XInput: thumbstick positive Y is up, and trigger and deadzone threshold constants exist.

findings.claim: Auto-switching by frontmost app in prior art matches on process path and/or window title, with a fallback policy. DS4Windows supports keyword modifiers (exact, ^prefix, suffix$, *contains) and 'Revert to Default Profile on Unknown'. JoyToKey lets the user choose the behaviour for non-associated apps.
findings.evidence: DS4Windows wiki: 'a match between a profile and process is defined using a process path and/or window title keywords'. Its keyword modifier syntax is described, and a debug log shows how titles matched. JoyToKey changelog: association by executable, later also by window title. Version 4.6 added the choice of behaviour when switching to a non-associated application. Xbox Accessories keeps 3 custom profiles plus a default on the controller and switches with the Profile button.

findings.claim: Very short synthetic taps are unreliable. Prior art enforces a minimum hold of about 20 ms for emitted taps and between macro keys.
findings.evidence: JoyToKey 'can now hold it for a minimum duration when the event emulation is not recognized reliably when you press the button too quickly (default 20 msec)'. reWASD recommends a delay between keys of 'at least a 20 milliseconds'. Inferred: a game polling once per 60 fps frame (16.7 ms), plus a cloud client sampling locally, can miss shorter taps.

findings.claim: Steam Input stacks on top of any virtual pad unless it is turned off for that controller type or game. reWASD users describe the chain 'physical → reWASD virtual → Steam remap' and Steam showing the same input twice. Steam's switches are the global 'Enable Steam Input for Xbox controllers' (Xbox Configuration Support) and the per-game 'Steam Input Per-Game Setting'.
findings.evidence: reWASD forum: Big Picture showed one input twice, as a DS4 and as an Xbox 360 device. Another post describes needing to account for both remapping layers. Steam community: Settings > Controller > Xbox Configuration Support = 'Enable Steam Input for Xbox controllers'; per game: Manage > Controller Options > Steam Input Per-Game Setting (Forced On/Off/global). The brief adds that Steam publishes its own 045E:028E 'GamePad-N', which SDL classifies as Steam-virtual when version == 0.

findings.claim: Seizing the SCUF gamepad interface also blocks OpenJoystickDriver and any other reader. OJD itself opens seize-first, so an OJD controller record for 1b1c:3a08 and GDHub's mapping engine cannot both own the device. The OJD route is an alternative to GDHub's engine, not an output sink for it, unless OJD's dext exposes an injection API.
findings.evidence: Brief §4a: OJD 'opens seize-first, falling back to shared'; com.openjoystickdriver.XboxUSBDevice 0.5.0-beta.4 is active (systemextensionsctl list). The IOHIDLibUserClient seize semantics above apply to whichever process seizes first. No evidence was found of an OJD user-client API for third-party report injection.

findings.claim: The existing SwiftUI controller view already has what assign-by-click needs: a hotspot per control on all four views (including back paddles and side SAX), live active, stick and trigger rendering, and callout labels. Only the tap action and the label text need to change by mode.
findings.evidence: ControllerSideView builds HotspotView(control:, active: mapping.isActive, stick:, trigger:, onTap: { if !editor.isEditing { device.startLearn(controlId:) } }). CalloutLayer draws per-control labels with leader lines and colour states. ControlLayout.Side has front/back/sideLeft/sideRight. Package targets macOS 14, so SwiftUI .inspector is available.

implications_for_design: ARCHITECTURE SPLIT. Keep ControlMapping and LearnSession as the INPUT-decoding layer: HID field to physical control id, with calibration ranges and physicalBits. Add an OUTPUT layer: Profile, then Layer, then ControlBinding, then Activator, then Action, plus Macros. New files: Sources/GDHub/Engine/{PhysicalSnapshot.swift, EchoResolver.swift, AnalogConditioner.swift, ActivatorMachine.swift, MacroPlayer.swift, Scheduler.swift, OutputAccumulator.swift, MappingCore.swift, MappingEngine.swift}, Sources/GDHub/Output/{OutputSink.swift, KeyboardMouseSink.swift, VirtualPadSink.swift}, Sources/GDHub/Profiles/{Profile.swift, ProfileStore.swift, ProfileRouter.swift, Macro.swift, MacroRecorder.swift}. Profiles live at ~/Library/Application Support/GDHub/profiles/<uuid>.json plus profiles/index.json (rules order, defaultProfileId, fallback policy). Use atomic writes and keep the last 40 backups, as ControlLayout.saveAsUserLayout already does.

PHYSICAL SNAPSHOT (engine input). struct PhysicalSnapshot { var t: UInt64 /*mach ticks from the IOHID timestamp callback*/; var digital: Set<ControlID>; var triggers: [ControlID: Double] /*0...1 calibrated*/; var sticks: [ControlID: SIMD2<Double>] /*-1...1, x right+, y down+ like the existing code; sinks convert to XInput y-up+*/ }. Build it from GamepadFrame + ControlMapping. EchoResolver runs first: each paddle or SAX physical bit is a digital control in its own right, and a standard button or hat direction that rises within a window of N reports (start N=2, tune by capture) of an extra-bit rising edge is attributed to that paddle and removed from the face control until the paddle is released (B3Mac edge rule). Prefer suppressing only the learned echo target (ControlMapping.buttons[paddleId], e.g. hat 2 for paddle_outer_right). Fall back to suppressing everything that rose when the learned target is stale, e.g. after an onboard profile change. Use the same resolver for UI lighting so pressing SAX-left no longer lights A.

DATA MODEL (Codable, explicit discriminator; do NOT reuse the synthesized `{"button":{"_0":1}}` style). typealias ControlID = String (layout ids). struct Profile: Codable, Identifiable { var schemaVersion = 1; var id: UUID; var name: String; var device = "envision-pro"; var match: [AppRule]; var outputMode: OutputMode /* .keyboardMouse | .xbox | .mixed */; var timing: TimingDefaults /* tapHoldMs 30, longPressMs 300, doubleTapMs 250, turboPeriodMs 80, hysteresis 0.03 */; var layers: [Layer] /* layers[0] = base */; var macros: [Macro]; var hidePhysicalController: Bool /* seize */ }. struct AppRule: Codable { var bundleId: String; var windowTitle: String? /* regex, needs AX */ }. struct Layer: Codable, Identifiable { var id: String; var name: String; var color: String; var releaseHeldOnEnter = false /* Steam action-layer style when true, mode-shift style when false */; var bindings: [ControlID: ControlBinding] /* sparse: a missing key inherits from the next active layer down */ }. enum ControlBinding: Codable { case digital(DigitalBinding) /* buttons, paddles, SAX, D-pad, G-keys, profile */; case trigger(TriggerBinding); case stick(StickBindingOut); case block /* reWASD 'Do not inherit' */ }.

ACTIVATORS AND ACTIONS (Steam semantics plus reWASD Triple). struct DigitalBinding: Codable { var activators: [Activator] }. struct Activator: Codable, Identifiable { var id: UUID; var on: ActivatorKind /* .press | .start | .release | .long(ms:) | .double(windowMs:) | .triple(windowMs:) | .chord(with: ControlID) */; var actions: [Action] /* fired together */; var toggle = false; var turbo: Turbo? /* periodMs, dutyPct */; var interruptible = true; var startDelayMs = 0; var endDelayMs = 0; var cycle = false /* fire one action per activation, round-robin */; var cycleResetMs: Int? /* AntiMicroX auto-reset */ }. enum Action: Codable { case pad(PadButton) /* a b x y lb rb view menu guide share ls rs dpadUp dpadDown dpadLeft dpadRight */; case padAxis(PadAxis, value: Double, mode: AxisMode /* .absolute | .relative */) /* lx ly rx ry lt rt */; case key(KeyChord) /* macOS kVK virtual keycode (physical position, layout-independent) + modifiers; Xbox Accessories allows 1 non-modifier + any modifiers, GDHub may allow more */; case mouseButton(MouseButton); case scroll(dx: Int, dy: Int) /* notches */; case macro(UUID); case layer(String, LayerMode /* .hold | .toggle | .oneShot | .switchBase */); case profile(ProfileSwitch /* .next | .previous | .id(UUID) */); case passthrough /* emit the control's native Xbox function */; case none }. Resolution rules: if the binding has only .press/.start/.release, fire on the edge with zero added latency. When .long, .double or .triple exist, interruptible .press activators are held back and either emitted as a tap of tapHoldMs if released before the window ends, or dropped when the long press fires (Steam). Non-interruptible .press fires immediately in addition. .start fires first and .release last (reWASD). Show a latency badge in the UI on any control whose binding needs disambiguation.

ANALOG. struct StickBindingOut: Codable { var mode: StickMode /* .pad(PadStick, swap:Bool) | .directions(DirectionConfig) | .mouse(MouseConfig) | .scroll(ScrollConfig) | .flick(FlickConfig) later | .none */; var deadzone = Deadzone(inner: 0.08, outer: 0.97, shape: .scaledRadial /* .radial | .axial | .square */); var antiDeadzone = 0.0 /* pad output only */; var curve: Curve = .linear; var sensitivity = 1.0; var invertX = false; var invertY = false; var ring: RingBinding? /* Steam outer ring / AntiMicroX Distance, e.g. radius 0.9 to Shift = run */ }. struct DirectionConfig { var ways: Int /* 4 or 8 */; var diagonalRangeDeg = 45.0; var threshold = 0.35; var up, down, left, right: DigitalBinding; var zones: [DistanceZone]? }. Stick directions become virtual ControlIDs like "left_stick.up", so WASD, arrows or a D-pad are ordinary digital bindings with activators. enum Curve: Codable { case linear, enhancedPrecision /* AntiMicroX 0.405x below 40% */, quadratic, cubic, easeOutQuad, power(Double), bezier(x1:Double,y1:Double,x2:Double,y2:Double) /* DS4Windows custom */ }. MouseConfig { speedPxPerSec 1500; accelRampMs 0 /* AntiMicroX easing 750 */; subpixel accumulation }. struct TriggerBinding { var output: TriggerOutput /* .pad(.lt/.rt) | .none */; var deadzone = 0.02; var maxZone = 0.98; var curve: Curve; var softPoint = 0.30; var fullPoint = 0.95; var soft: DigitalBinding?; var full: DigitalBinding?; var hipFire: HipFire /* .off | .normal(ms) | .exclusive(ms) per Steam */; var analogWhenDigitalBound = true }. Calibrate first with the learned AxisRange in ControlMapping.sticks[...].ranges and a per-trigger max (wireless LT/RT peak about 1010–1023 per the brief). Defaults: for .pad output use a small inner deadzone (0–5%) so it does not stack with the game's own XInput-style deadzone; for keys and mouse GDHub's deadzone is the only one, so use 15–20% for directions and about 8% for mouse (Sutphin's 0.1–0.2 range).

MACROS. struct Macro: Codable, Identifiable { var id: UUID; var name: String; var steps: [MacroStep]; var mode: MacroMode /* .executeAtOnce (runs to completion) | .holdUntilRelease (abort and release everything on trigger release; reWASD) */; var repeatPolicy: MacroRepeat /* .once | .count(n) | .whileHeld | .toggle (until pressed again) */; var repeatGapMs = 0 /* reWASD pause between iterations */; var stepGapMs = 0 /* default delay between keys; editor warns below 20 ms */; var retrigger: Retrigger /* .ignore (default) | .restart | .queueOne | .stop */; var cancelOnLayerChange = false; var cancelOnProfileChange = true /* always forced */ }. enum MacroStep: Codable { case down(OutputKey), up(OutputKey), tap(OutputKey, holdMs: Int), wait(ms: Int), waitForNextPress /* reWASD combo break */, axis(PadAxis, value: Double, mode: AxisMode, holdMs: Int?), mouseMove(dx: Int, dy: Int, overMs: Int), scroll(dx: Int, dy: Int), text(String) /* CGEventKeyboardSetUnicodeString */, rumble(ms: Int, strength: Double) /* later: output report 0x09 */, layer(String, LayerMode), loop(count: Int, steps: [MacroStep]), releaseAll }. enum OutputKey: Hashable, Codable { case pad(PadButton), key(UInt16), mouse(MouseButton) }. Ownership rule: each running macro instance owns the outputs it pressed and releases all of them when it stops, aborts or is interrupted. Outputs are reference-counted across sources (see Runtime), so a macro and a direct binding pressing the same key do not cut each other off. MacroRecorder: records controller edges from PhysicalSnapshot timestamps and turns them into down/up/wait steps, with 'record delays' and quantize options (1/5/10 ms), trimming leading and trailing idle, and an optional 'merge short down/up into tap' (DS4Windows Record delays / Play once / Repeat while held; reWASD Start recording). Recording keyboard and mouse is opt-in: it needs a listen-only CGEventTap and the Input Monitoring (ListenEvent) permission, and must ignore events GDHub itself posted (tagged with kCGEventSourceUserData = 'GDHU').

RUNTIME AND TIMING. (1) Change HIDMonitor to call IOHIDDeviceSetDispatchQueue(engineQueue) and IOHIDDeviceRegisterInputReportWithTimeStampCallback, then IOHIDDeviceActivate. Remove the run-loop scheduling, because the header forbids using both. engineQueue = serial, QoS .userInteractive. Parsing and the engine run there; only throttled snapshots (≤60–125 Hz, matching the existing 8 ms publish) go to the MainActor for UI and logs. (2) The core is a pure value type: struct MappingCore { mutating func step(_ input: PhysicalSnapshot?, now: UInt64) -> [OutputEvent] }. It makes every decision from report timestamps, never from wall-clock at execution, so replaying recorded frames gives byte-identical output. Write golden tests from scuf-envision captures and Scufpad fixtures. (3) Order within each tick: decode, echo-resolve, condition analog, derive virtual digital inputs (stick directions, ring, trigger soft/full with hysteresis), detect edges, resolve each edge's binding against the active layer stack AT PRESS TIME (the binding instance owns the press until release, so layer changes never strand or retrigger held outputs unless layer.releaseHeldOnEnter is set), run activator state machines, pop due Scheduler items from a min-heap keyed by due time (turbo phases, delayed taps, macro steps), feed OutputAccumulator, diff, then send to sinks. (4) A DispatchSourceTimer(flags: .strict, 1 ms, leeway 0) on engineQueue runs the scheduler between reports. Suspend it when nothing is scheduled or held. (5) OutputAccumulator: refcount per OutputKey from source ids (emit down on 0→1 and up on 1→0); per-axis contributions (base from stick passthrough, .relative adds, latest .absolute overrides, clamp); per-tick sums of mouse delta and scroll. (6) Failsafes: releaseAll() on no input report for 150 ms (Scuf2Switch uses a 250 ms freshness gate), on receiver 3a08→3a09, device removal, profile switch, sleep/screen lock (NSWorkspace notifications), app quit, and an emergency chord (hold View+Menu+Profile 2 s) that disables mapping and passes through (reWASD emergency remap-off). Target latency for direct bindings is report arrival to event post in under 1 ms; only controls with long/double/triple activators add their window.

OUTPUT SINKS. protocol OutputSink: AnyObject { func apply(_ diff: OutputDiff, at t: UInt64); func releaseAll(); var capabilities: SinkCaps { get } }. KeyboardMouseSink (available now, no developer account): CGEventSource(stateID: .hidSystemState); post at .cghidEventTap; tag every event with kCGEventSourceUserData. Send modifiers as flagsChanged events and keep cumulative CGEventFlags on later key events. For mouse moves, post kCGEventMouseMoved, or the matching Dragged type while a button is held, with location = current + delta clamped to the display and kCGMouseEventDeltaX/Y set, keeping a subpixel remainder. Send scroll as line units (one per notch). Check permission with CGPreflightPostEventAccess and request it with CGRequestPostEventAccess on first enable. VirtualPadSink is a protocol with implementations chosen by the virtual-gamepad workstream: CoreHIDPadSink (entitled), DextPadSink (dev-signed or distributed dext), each with a ReportBuilder for the chosen identity (045E:0B13 dual collection or 028E with version ≠ 0, per brief §4b). Send on change plus a keepalive (start at ≤250 Hz; verify what the publisher tolerates). Converts y-down to the target's convention (XInput: positive Y = up). Mixed mode routes each Action to the sink that supports it. The engine must not depend on which sink exists, so the keyboard path ships first and the Xbox path plugs in later.

HIDE PHYSICAL CONTROLLER AND STEAM INPUT POLICY. (a) Add a per-profile 'Hide physical controller' setting, on by default in .xbox and .mixed modes and recommended in .keyboardMouse mode. When set, GDHub opens the FF58 gamepad interface with kIOHIDOptionsTypeSeize, so Steam, GeForce NOW and Shadow (all SDL/IOHIDLib readers) stop seeing the raw SCUF. Without this they get double input, or a game toggles its glyphs between controller and keyboard. Optionally seize the Consumer interface too, so G2/G3/G4 stop changing system volume when they are remapped (brief §6.8). Show a warning that this also locks out OpenJoystickDriver and iCUE. (b) Recommended default with a GDHub virtual Xbox pad: GDHub owns all mapping. In Steam, turn off 'Enable Steam Input for Xbox controllers' (Settings > Controller), or set the game's Steam Input Per-Game Setting to Disabled, so Steam does not remap GDHub's output a second time. (c) If the user wants Steam Input (community configs, gyro), offer a 'Steam passthrough' profile: face buttons, sticks and triggers 1:1, with paddles, SAX and G-keys on Xbox buttons or keys, since no Xbox identity carries paddles. (d) Warn that Steam keeps per-GUID SDL_GamepadBind entries in config.vdf, which already exist on this Mac, and that a stale entry for the virtual pad's GUID will scramble buttons. (e) Cloud clients (GeForce NOW, Shadow) are not Steam, so only (a) applies. Build an in-app checklist page per host covering Steam, GeForce NOW and Shadow.

PROFILES AND AUTO-SWITCH. A MainActor ProfileRouter observes NSWorkspace.shared.notificationCenter didActivateApplicationNotification and evaluates rules in order: bundleId (com.valvesoftware.steam; com.nvidia.gfnpc.mall; Shadow's stream window com.blade.shadow-macos and shell com.electron.shadow), then an optional windowTitle regex. Reading titles needs Accessibility: AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid) → kAXFocusedWindowAttribute → kAXTitleAttribute. Make it opt-in, since full Accessibility is broader than PostEvent. Fallback setting: 'Revert to default profile' or 'Keep last profile' (DS4Windows, JoyToKey). A manual pin from the menu bar or toolbar overrides the rules. Action.profile(.next) can be bound to G-keys; leave the physical Profile button (button 17) unbound by default because it also switches the onboard profile. Switch procedure on engineQueue: releaseAll(), swap the CompiledProfile, and latch every currently held control so it is ignored until released. A rules debug log shows which bundle id and title matched (as in DS4Windows).

COMPILATION AND VALIDATION. The MainActor edits Profile values. Before handing a profile to the engine (engineQueue.async), compile it into an immutable CompiledProfile: flatten layers into per-control lookup tables, precompute needsDisambiguation per control, resolve macro references and detect cycles (a macro calling itself through loop or layer), make sure every toggle or Custom-style layer has a way back to base (reWASD warns about getting stuck), clamp timings, and map ControlIDs to bit masks for speed. Reject or flag invalid profiles in the UI rather than at runtime.

UI (reuse ControllerView). Add a mode picker: Live | Learn | Assign. In Assign mode, HotspotView.onTap sets selectedControl instead of calling device.startLearn, and a macOS 14 .inspector panel shows the editor for that control in the current layer: an activator list (+ Press / Long / Double / Triple / Start / Release / Chord), an action picker (Xbox button grid, key capture field, mouse, macro, layer, profile), and toggle, turbo, delay and interruptible controls. A stick hotspot opens a mode picker plus a deadzone and curve editor drawn over the live stick dot (inner and outer rings, direction sectors). A trigger hotspot opens soft/full markers over the existing fill bar. Callout labels show the action summary per control (e.g. 'P1 → R / hold: Shift 1') in the colour of the shown layer (reWASD colours its layers). A layer bar shows Base / Shift 1..n, and while a hold-layer control is physically held the view previews that layer live. A Profiles sheet holds the app rules editor and import/export. The macro editor sheet has a reorderable step list, Record from controller, and a test-play button whose output appears in a new Output Monitor next to InputMonitorView. A permissions banner covers PostEvent, plus Input Monitoring and Accessibility only when those opt-in features are used. Mockups go in /docs/mockups per the user's rules.

SIGNING AND ACCOUNTS (covers both cases). Keyboard and mouse output, profiles, macros and seizing need no paid account. Do sign bundle.sh output with a stable identity (a free Personal Team 'Apple Development' certificate via Xcode, or a self-signed code-signing certificate) instead of the ad-hoc 'codesign --sign -', so the PostEvent grant survives rebuilds. The Xbox output sink depends on the virtual-gamepad route. Without a paid account the options are a CoreHID publisher in a SIP+AMFI-off VM, or the OJD-record route, which bypasses GDHub's engine. With a paid account, a dev-signed dext publishing USB transport, or the CoreHID entitlement request.

P0 Engine plumbing, no behaviour change: dispatch-queue and timestamped HID input, PhysicalSnapshot, EchoResolver (fixes A lighting when SAX is pressed), throttled UI snapshots, golden-test harness replaying captures. P1 Keyboard mapping, usable today in Steam, GeForce NOW and Shadow: Profile/Layer/DigitalBinding with .press only, Actions key/mouseButton/scroll, KeyboardMouseSink with PostEvent permission flow, stick→directions (WASD) and stick→mouse, trigger soft/full thresholds, hide-physical seize, releaseAll failsafes and emergency chord, Assign-mode UI with inspector, stable signing. P2 Full activators: long/double/triple/start/release/chord, toggle, turbo, start/end delays, interruptible, cycle, hold/toggle/oneShot layers with inheritance and block, deterministic scheduler with tests. P4 Auto-switch: NSWorkspace rules, opt-in AX window-title rules, fallback policy, menu-bar profile pin, profile cycling from G-keys. P5 Xbox mapping: VirtualPadSink integration once the publisher route lands (it can move ahead of P3/P4 if the publisher is ready first), pad buttons and axes, anti-deadzone, Steam passthrough profile, per-host checklist (Steam Input off, stale SDL_GamepadBind warning).
